title: MATH-FIX: is the MATH corpus's near-zero accuracy a capability result or an answer-extraction artefact, and what does correcting it do to the router? (zero calls)
question: Tolerant extractor (last \boxed / 'final answer is' / last number, any candidate may match), normalisation with numeric tolerance 1e-6; correction only ever RAISES; corrected column written to a new table, ingested rows untouched; then MC-E2E re-run on the overlay. (1) per-model corrected accuracy + count of responses with no extractable answer; (2) do the six 0.000 models rise above 0.10; (3) the deployed router gain on corrected data, three seeds. Predictions: zeros rise to 0.3-0.7; gain shrinks to +2 to +3.5pp.

plain_description.what: Re-scores MATH answers with a more tolerant answer extractor. It accepts the last boxed answer, 'final answer is' or the last number, with numeric tolerance, and it only ever raises scores. Then it re-runs the routing evaluation on the corrected data. No calls.
plain_description.why: Six models scored near 0 on MATH. That looked like an answer-extraction artefact rather than real inability, and it could inflate the measured routing gain.
plain_description.information: If zeros jump, the old numbers were artefacts and the routing gain must be re-estimated. Result: done, artefact confirmed. 21.7% of cells were corrected, and several models went from about 0 to 0.40-0.60. Routing per cell still helps in every seed, but less: +2.7 points on average instead of +5.0. A later re-read on the tree's own held-out pool gave about +3.4. That figure was itself replaced by a clean re-measurement of about +2.9, with policies fitted on training questions only. Pool separation was checked by question id only, not by content.
